refined_nucleus: The micro-machined sensor's interaction with the PPG sensor substrate is optimized through a novel thermal expansion coefficient matching and material selection, enabled by a 3D printing technology.
new_relationship: The relationship between the micro-machined sensor's interaction with the PPG sensor substrate and the 3D printing technology enables the optimization of the thermal expansion coefficient matching and material selection.
new_configuration: The 3D printing technology is used to create a customized PPG sensor substrate with an embedded micro-machined sensor.
new_control_rule: The control unit is programmed to adjust the thermal expansion coefficient matching and material selection based on real-time sensor data.
refined_structure: The proposed device consists of a 3D printed PPG sensor substrate with an embedded micro-machined sensor, a control unit, and a power source.
refined_causal_chain: Failure: SpO2 sensor drift at low perfusion
Cause: Reduced signal quality under low perfusion conditions
Intervention: Embedding the micro-machined sensor using 3D printing technology
Mechanism: Augmenting the PPG sensor's performance through thermal expansion coefficient matching and material selection
remaining_risks: The effectiveness of the 3D printing technology in creating a customized PPG sensor substrate with an embedded micro-machined sensor is still to be demonstrated.
